_comment: Editable mappings for app/legal_preprocessor.py. Delete any key to fall back to the built-in default; add a key to override it. Loaded once at startup with json.load(), and a missing or malformed file is non-fatal - the module falls back to the defaults compiled into it.

abbreviations.AMOSUP: Associated Marine Officers' and Seamen's Union of the Philippines
abbreviations._caution: The next group came from a clinical/general corpus, not from Philippine case law. They are inert on legal text in most cases but will fire on the words below, so delete the ones you do not want. CT, ILO and CBA in particular are common enough in unrelated writing to misfire.
abbreviations._caution_2: These are corporate names. They expand only as standalone words, so they are usually safe, but they will rewrite a party name that happens to appear alone on a line - set the value to the key itself to neutralise one.

currency_aliases._comment: How amounts are written in practice. Philippine decisions almost never say 'PHP' - they write 'P' or the peso sign - so without these aliases the currency pass misses nearly every real amount. The digit string that follows is what gets spelled out.

ocr_map._comment: Digit-for-letter confusions from the scanner, matched on word boundaries only. The spec named 1s and prope1iies; th1s, 1t and wa1s are added because they are the most frequent equivalents in scanned opinions and cost nothing. Add your own here.
